id: Money For Old Rope-San Fran, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Money For Old Rope
long_description:
Wellington classic rock cover favourites celebrate 10 years of anthems with a massive free anniversary gig at San Fran.

To celebrate a decade of tearing up the local music scene, Wellington’s premier classic rock covers band are throwing the ultimate birthday bash. Money For Old Rope are marking their 10th Anniversary by doing what they do best — delivering a high-energy, no-holds-barred night of classic rock hits, completely free of charge.

Taking over Wellington's iconic San Fran on Sunday 8th November, this special milestone show promises to be an absolute night for the ages. Entry is 100% free, giving back to the local fans, friends, and rock devotees who have supported the band's journey over the last ten years.

Formed a decade ago, Money For Old Rope have become a staple of the lower north island's live music circuit. Known for their electrifying stage presence and an unrelenting setlist of the greatest rock anthems ever written, the band has spent ten years filling dance floors, shaking pub rafters, and cementing their reputation as the region's go-to classic rock covers experience.

When we first put the band together ten years ago, we just wanted to play the loud, timeless classic rock music we loved, says the band. To still be doing it a decade later, seeing the same incredible energy from our audience week after week is something pretty special. What better way could we possibly celebrate this milestone than by throwing a massive, free party at San Fran and reliving ten years of rock'n'roll memories with everyone?

Doors open for this unforgettable Sunday session on Sunday 8th November at 5pm. Because entry is completely free, fans are encouraged to get in early to secure their spot on the dance floor before the venue reaches capacity.

id: Moon Jam Nite-MOON, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Moon Jam Nite
long_description:
Get your 15 minutes of fame at Newtown's famous Moon Jam Nite, every Tuesday from 7.30pm

The evening starts off as a regular open mic, and transforms into a full on jam towards the end.

Put your moniker into the sign up sheet, and own your time slot. You can call upon the many talented muso's available to help you play your slot.

A full stage with electric guitar, bass, keyboard, drums, mics, lights and full support from our sound tech.

Bring your own songs, poems, and friends (and make some new ones too)

id: April Phillips At The Cabletop!-Cable Top Eatery, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: April Phillips At The Cabletop!
long_description:
April performs solo with professional high quality backing tracks - get the big band sound with intimacy and elegance of a solo class act.

Her forte is jazz and blues and she has appeared in many jazz festivals throughout New Zealand. Jazz reviewers have described her as having “a voice of honey” and she has been compared to Diana Krall and Ella Fitzgerald.

Experience breathtaking harbour views from our eatery, situated atop the car alongside a stunning garden deck. We celebrate our love for Jazz by hosting Live at Five every Wednesday night. Join us for an unforgettable evenings filled with great music and atmosphere

id: Condenser Play The Cure And Joy Division-MOON, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Condenser Play The Cure And Joy Division
long_description:
Condenser are Wellington punk rock stalwarts who've been kicking against the pricks since 1980. The trio — James on drums, PJ on bass, and Nigel on guitar — deliver a raw, high-energy sound rooted in the genre's incendiary origins.
But Condenser is more than a band. James, Nigel, and PJ are all veterans of the Wellington scene, having cut their teeth in noted acts including Condemned Sector, Neoteric Tribesmen, the Resurrectionists and Compos Mentis — groups that helped shape the Wellington sound and foster a spirit of rebellion that still resonates today.
AT this gig you can expect a tightly packed set of classic covers:
The Cure's first album Boys Don't Cry (1979), and
Joy Divisions seminal album Unknown Pleasures

Condenser don't just perform punk and post-punk, they carry its living history, connecting the dots between Wellington's punk past and its present, and keeping the flame burning bright in New Zealand.

Supported by our good friends, the amazingly talented Los Punkys, with their crazy blend of high energy latin punk fusion.

id: Miro Holland Group-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Miro Holland Group
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Miro Holland Group!

New takes on Miro's compositions, returning to Undercurrent with a different instrumentation and a little more life lived -expect wild and various plumes of colour.

In their first return performance since Wellington Jazz Festival's 'Song for Iqbal, Song for Pat'- and continuing their acclaimed year of international performance- Miro Holland Group breaks down the intention of their composed melodies, and displays more their nuances in today's performance. 

Featuring regular collaborators Miro Holland, Ateo Buhne, and Theo Thompson, and special guests; Daniel Yeabsley and Sylvester Green.

Plus, for the first time in Aotearoa, the group's unreleased live album will be for sale.

Be there!

$15

id: Negative Approach 2026 AUS & NZ Tour-Valhalla, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Negative Approach 2026 AUS & NZ Tour
long_description:
Check it out!

At long last, one of the most vital bands to ever help start the movement are finally bringing their legacy-level, household hardcore anthems to Aus & NZ!

Negative Approach. Yep, that one. Formed back in 81 and thought to be gone soon after, NA left us a short but permanent set of songs that still stand strong above the majority to this day.

Reformed again only in 06, they pummelled their way right back through with even more fury than round 1. No cash grab reunion, no bullshit, just vital hardcore for the ages here in full force. Be there or remain irrelevant.


Supports:
Christchurch
Supported by Radium, Kisser & Fastplant

Wellington
Supported by Noxo, No Sector & Unsanitary Napkin

Auckland
Supported by Dick Move & Another Fucking Problem
